text:
Marathon Petroleum climbed 0.51% today to close at $384.97, extending a sharp 6.71% rally over the past two weeks. The move reflects a combination of rising crude prices—U.S. oil touched near $90 a barrel on Middle East tensions—and exceptionally tight refinery conditions, with U.S. refineries running at 97.4% capacity. When refineries are operating at peak utilization against strong crude prices, refiners' profit margins tend to widen because they can run fuel output continuously while converting cheaper crude into more valuable products.

The geopolitical risks driving oil higher are real and ongoing: Iran struck targets in Kuwait, Jordan, and Bahrain in retaliation for U.S. strikes on Iranian military sites, while tankers were damaged near the Strait of Hormuz—a critical chokepoint where 17 million barrels transit daily. These supply-side risks support sustained crude prices, which benefit a large independent refiner like Marathon Petroleum as long as refinery utilization stays high.
